messages:
natalie: Heads-up: onboarding TidalWave's LoRA merge. Pushed a quick sanity pack to S3 — ran baseline smoke locally and saw a couple odd numeric truncation cases. Can we do a compatibility check + quant sanity? cc @vik @chris
chris: 👍 can you drop the quickpack link and the run command?
natalie: Link: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/tidalwave/tidalwave_quickpack_v1.tar.gz
run command we used: `./run_quickpack.sh --model merged-lora-v1 --quant int4 --seed 42 --evalset billing_examples.json`
vik: I pulled and ran the pack on a small batch (50 cases). Overall pass 91% but 2 fails that look like decimal/amount formatting (e.g., "$12.00" -> "12" or split tokens). Log snippet:
```
[2024-11-03 15:05:12] prompt_id=TW_042 case=invoice_amount input="Total due: $12.00" output="Total due: 12"
[2024-11-03 15:05:12] prompt_id=TW_047 case=invoice_amount input="Balance: USD 7.50" output="Balance: USD 7 . 5 0"
```
vik: tags: tokenizer-v2.2.9, quant-profile=int4-default
nina: are those tokenizer tokenization artifacts or quant-induced tokenization drift? looks like tokens are splitting punctuation under int4 kernel in the downstream decode
eval-bot: Quickpack run complete (id=qk-1749123456-run1). metrics: BLEU=0.72, EM=0.89, hallucination_rate=0.03, slow_tail=0.4%. regressions vs baseline: answer_sanity -0.02, decimal_format -0.12
shahzad: repro steps: run with fp16 on same merged-lora-v1 -> decimal issues disappear. So likely quantization affecting decode logits around punctuation tokens. quick repro:
```
# fp16
python3 infer.py --model merged-lora-v1 --quant fp16 --prompt "Total due: $12.00"
# int4
python3 infer.py --model merged-lora-v1 --quant int4 --prompt "Total due: $12.00"
```
shahzad: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) pin tokenizer to 2.3.1 (some fixes for punctuation BPE), 2) try per-channel quant + outlier-clipping, 3) add a postprocess numeric normalizer in customer's eval pipeline to avoid formatting regressions being counted as fail
natalie: I can try repacking with tokenizer 2.3.1 and a peppered int4 profile (outlier clip=2.5). Will push new quickpack and re-run overnight.
lex: good call. Also file a product note: customers that rely on strict numeric formats (billing, receipts) should default to fp16/dedicated profile or enable numeric postprocessing. @product
chris: ping once new quickpack is up and we can run a full smoke across 1k cases. I can spin up the dedicated test pool for that
eval-bot: New quickpack run started by natalie (run_id=qk-1749123499-run2)
natalie: thanks all — I'll upload updated tarball and post results in this thread when done :thumbsup:
